key_insight: Adding ADR-based physics to TSMixer showed no consistent benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting over the purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, added physics-model complexity may offer limited practical value beyond a modern neural baseline.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Test two hybrid architectures using feature augmentation and residual learning.
Compare convergence, forecast accuracy, geographic transferability, and data efficiency.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries suggested slightly faster training convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed approaches or solar-cell design tasks.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
